topic: Diagnosing React effects that rerun because object dependencies change identity

hook.headline: Your Effect dependency may change every render
hook.hook: An object created during rendering has a new identity, so an Effect depending on it can reconnect after unrelated renders.
hook.visualCaption: React compares each dependency with its previous value using Object.is after a commit.
hook.microExample: new object → dependency changed → cleanup → setup

mentalModel.title: Identity drives dependency changes
mentalModel.coreIdea: React compares each Effect dependency with its previous value using Object.is. A freshly created object is a different reference, even when its fields match, so the Effect can run cleanup and setup again after a commit.
mentalModel.keyOutcome: Dependency identity can cause extra synchronization even when the underlying business value did not change.
mentalModel.mentalShortcut: render → new reference → Object.is false → effect reruns

code.title: Create options inside the Effect
code.intro: Depend on the primitive values that actually control the external synchronization.
code.highlightReason: The Effect now depends on primitive values instead of an options object recreated during rendering.
code.takeaway: Restructure the Effect so its dependency list reflects the reactive values that genuinely control synchronization.
code.professionalNote: Do not remove required dependencies merely to suppress reruns; change the surrounding code so the dependency is unnecessary.

production.title: Unexpected reconnects after harmless UI updates
production.scenario: A websocket Effect depends on a render-created options object. Typing into unrelated local state re-renders the component, producing a new options reference and reconnecting the socket.
problems: Cleanup closes a healthy connection and setup opens another even though serverUrl and roomId are unchanged.
Extra reconnects can obscure the trigger because the object contents look identical in logs.
production.professionalApproach: Inspect dependencies across consecutive renders. Use Object.is to identify the changing value, then remove unnecessary object creation from the dependency boundary rather than disabling exhaustive-deps.
production.debugClue: Logged option fields are unchanged, but Object.is(previousOptions, currentOptions) returns false across renders.

interview.question: Why can a React Effect rerun when an object dependency appears to contain exactly the same values?
interview.answer: React compares Effect dependencies with their previous values using Object.is. Two separately created objects are different references, even if their properties match, so React treats that dependency as changed. I usually remove unnecessary object dependencies by creating the object inside the Effect and depending on the primitive reactive values it actually uses.
